decision_briefs.title: Genre coverage: how do we stop the benchmark being 99.6% hadith?
decision_briefs.blocks: Every measured number in the project. Nothing generalizes past hadith until this is answered, and the benchmark cannot be frozen.
decision_briefs.question: The draft benchmark is 1,107 hadith items out of 1,111. Where does genre diversity actually come from?
decision_briefs.why_now: This gates the benchmark rebuild, and the rebuild gates re-running the bakeoff and QE study. Deciding it late means paying for those runs twice.
evidence: 1,107 of 1,111 draft_test items are LK Hadith; ATHAR contributes 4. Zero tafsir, philosophy, adab, history, poetry.

ATHAR's parquet files carry ONLY (arabic, english) columns — no per-row work, author, or genre metadata exists. Verified against both train and test schemas (src/versed_translator/benchmark/assemble.py:20).
ATHAR's median item is 18 Arabic words, below the benchmark's own 30-word band floor — that, not a sampling bug, is why only 4 rows survived.
Hadith is unusually formulaic (isnad chains, fixed openings). A model that handles it well may fail on Sufi metaphor or legal reasoning and we would not see it.

options.label: Email the ATHAR author for per-work/genre provenance
options.detail: Combine with the D1d license question — one email, two possible unlocks. Costs nothing and may hand us the genre axis outright. Does not block starting (b) in parallel.

options.label: Add a sub-30-word band so ATHAR's diversity counts
options.detail: Cheap interim fix. Gets ATHAR's sentence-level material into the benchmark immediately, but genre labels stay coarse until (a) answers.

options.label: Accept hadith-only for v0.1; get genre via PD alignment in v0.2
options.detail: Honest and already labeled that way. But it pulls C7 (Versed Align) forward, which is a genuinely bigger scope — take it deliberately, never by drift.

decision_briefs.recommendation: Do (a) immediately and (b) as the interim. Treat (c) as the deliberate v0.2 path, not something an agent session backs into.

decision_briefs.title: Make structured block translation with ID preservation the production contract?
decision_briefs.blocks: The C5 router design, and the worst known safety gap in the whole system.
decision_briefs.question: Should production always translate in ID-preserving structured blocks, so a dropped block is directly observable?
decision_briefs.why_now: It is a one-line architectural decision that dissolves a failure mode no detector we have can catch. Deciding it before the router is built avoids designing detection for a problem we can define away.
evidence: Partial clause removal is undetectable from (source, output) alone on unpunctuated classical Arabic: sentence_ratio_flag cannot run and a truncated output stays inside the normal Arabic→English expansion band.
COMETKiwi also misses it — 22.9% detection, and a NEGATIVE mean delta, meaning it scores truncated text HIGHER than the complete translation.
So neither the neural signal nor the deterministic checks cover the single highest-severity omission failure. It is asserted as a known gap in tests/test_checks.py so it cannot regress silently.
The harness already supports the structured template — this costs implementation discipline, not new code.

options.label: Yes — structured blocks with IDs are the production contract
options.detail: A dropped or truncated block becomes structurally visible instead of semantically invisible. Cheaper than any detection scheme we could build.

options.label: No — keep free-form translation, invest in detection
options.detail: Means accepting that the highest-severity omission failure stays undetectable, or funding an LLM verifier pass to catch it.

decision_briefs.recommendation: Yes. It converts a detection problem we have measurably failed to solve into a structural property we get for free.

decision_briefs.title: Provision the remaining provider API keys, or formally descope the bakeoff field?
decision_briefs.blocks: Closing out C2 and ratifying D2a. Currently carried as ambient blockage, which is the worst of both.
decision_briefs.question: Do we get Gemini / Qwen-MT / DeepSeek keys, or do we record the bakeoff field as deliberately narrowed?
decision_briefs.why_now: Every session so far has listed 'no API keys' as a gap without either fixing it or dropping it. Either answer unblocks; carrying it does not.
evidence: TG27B (open, Modal H100) and Claude Sonnet 5 tied on hadith: chrF 50.24 vs 50.60, both 139/139 clean.
TG27B ran ~36x faster (0.68s vs 24.5s mean) at ~$0.27 for the whole set.
C8 requires an OPEN, fine-tunable base. Gemini / DeepSeek-API / Qwen-MT-API cannot be that regardless of their scores, so they do not actually compete for the production-translator slot.
The missing legs answer a different question — what a pure-API corpus route would cost — which only matters if fine-tuning fails at D8a.

options.label: Descope the field to TG27B / TG12B / Claude ceiling
options.detail: Record D2a as decided-by-field. Revisit the API route only if D8a (fine-tune GO/NO-GO) fails. Fastest path to a closed C2.

options.label: Provision the keys this week and run the full field
options.detail: Gives a complete comparison table and a real API-route cost baseline. Costs money and a session, and does not change the likely D2a outcome.

decision_briefs.recommendation: Descope, with the TG12B Modal leg still run — the 12B-vs-27B gap is the number that actually drives serving economics and has never been measured.

decision_briefs.title: ATHAR license conflict — which license is actually intended?
decision_briefs.blocks: Using ATHAR in the C8 training corpus. Currently held at eval-internal.
decision_briefs.question: ATHAR's dataset card says CC-BY-SA-4.0 in its YAML and CC-BY-NC-4.0 in its prose. Which governs?
decision_briefs.why_now: The same email should carry the D1e metadata question. One message, two unlocks — and the answer takes days to come back, so it should be out now.
evidence: ATHAR is the largest source we have: 66,043 pairs (65,043 train + 1,000 native test).
Card YAML says CC-BY-SA-4.0; card prose says CC-BY-NC-4.0. NC would bar it from anything Versed ships commercially.
Held at rights_status=eval_internal until resolved, so it is currently unusable for C8 training data.

options.label: Email the author now, combined with the D1e metadata question
options.detail: One message: which license is intended, and does per-work/genre provenance exist for the pairs?

options.label: Assume NC and keep it eval-internal permanently
options.detail: Safe but costs us the largest parallel source for training, and we never find out whether that was necessary.

decision_briefs.recommendation: Send the combined email. Assume NC in the meantime so nothing blocks on the reply.

decision_briefs.title: Approve and send the OpenITI letter
decision_briefs.blocks: Nothing immediately — but the answer takes weeks and gates commercial use, so lead time is the whole point.
decision_briefs.question: Is the drafted OpenITI letter approved to send?
decision_briefs.why_now: Drafted 2026-08-12 and still unsent. It is pure lead time: the reply arrives while we build, or it does not arrive and we learn that too.
evidence: Asks: we strip OpenITI markup/metadata and use only the underlying public-domain Arabic strings, most originating in pre-existing digital libraries; we create our own segmentation, translations, and audio. Is BY-NC-SA intended to cover those underlying strings or OpenITI's annotations and corpus-database? Would you grant Versed commercial permission for this public-access project?
Nothing in the roadmap blocks on the answer except commercial exploitation (D6b counsel is the other half).

options.label: Approve and send as drafted
options.detail: Starts the clock. The reply informs D6b (counsel) and the C12 release licensing.

options.label: Revise first — I want to change the framing
options.detail: Say what to change and it gets redrafted before sending.

decision_briefs.recommendation: Send as drafted. It is lead time we cannot buy back later.
